record.paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
record.context_brief: Integrality of integral-form Jack superpolynomial coefficients
record.original_question: Let J_Λ^(α) denote the integral form of the Jack superpolynomial indexed by a superpartition Λ, defined by J_Λ^(α)=v_Λ(α)P_Λ^(α), and let its monomial expansion be J_Λ^(α)=Σ_{Ω≤Λ} v_{ΛΩ}(α) m_Ω. Is it true that for every pair of superpartitions Ω≤Λ, each expansion coefficient v_{ΛΩ}(α) is a polynomial in α with integer coefficients, i.e. v_{ΛΩ}(α)∈ℤ[α]?

evidence.quote: We define the integral form of the Jack superpolynomials, to be denoted J^(α)_Λ, as (3.38) J^(α)_Λ = v_Λ(α)P^(α)_Λ,
When expanded in the monomial basis, i.e. (3.39) J^(α)_Λ = ∑_{Ω≤Λ} v_{ΛΩ}(α) m_Ω, where v_{ΛΛ}(α) = v_Λ(α), we have the following conjecture.
Conjecture 3.1 – [14] The coefficients v_{ΛΩ}(α) are polynomials in α with integer coefficients, that is, they belong to Z[α].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A superpartition is a pair $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$, where $\Lambda^a=(\Lambda_1,\dots,\Lambda_m)$ is a strictly decreasing sequence of non-negative integers and $\Lambda^s=(\Lambda_{m+1},\Lambda_{m+2},\dots)$ is a partition (weakly decreasing sequence of non-negative integers). Superpartitions index a basis of the ring of symmetric functions in superspace, which is the ring of polynomials in commuting variables $x_1,x_2,\dots$ and anticommuting variables $\theta_1,\theta_2,\dots$ that are invariant under the diagonal action of the symmetric group permuting simultaneously the $x_i$ and the $\theta_i$.

For each superpartition $\Lambda$, let $m_\Lambda$ denote the monomial symmetric function in superspace indexed by $\Lambda$. Equip the set of superpartitions of a fixed bidegree with the dominance order $\le$. The Jack symmetric functions in superspace $P^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda$ (depending on a parameter $\alpha$) are the unique basis characterized by:
(i) $P^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda = m_\Lambda + \sum_{\Omega<\Lambda} c_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)\, m_\Omega$,
(ii) orthogonality with respect to the natural one-parameter scalar product on superspace.

Define the integral form of the Jack superpolynomial by
$$J^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda(x;\theta) := v_\Lambda(\alpha)\, P^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda(x;\theta),$$
where $v_\Lambda(\alpha)$ is the natural normalization factor (the product over the cells of the diagram of $\Lambda$ of the appropriate hook-type linear factors in $\alpha$) that generalizes the classical normalization for Jack polynomials. Expanding in the monomial basis,
$$J^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda = \sum_{\Omega \le \Lambda} v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)\, m_\Omega,$$
with $v_{\Lambda\Lambda}(\alpha) = v_\Lambda(\alpha)$.

Question. Is it true that for every pair of superpartitions $\Omega \le \Lambda$, the coefficient $v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)$ is a polynomial in $\alpha$ with integer coefficients, i.e., $v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha) \in \mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface foundational works on Jack polynomials in superspace (e.g., the determinantal-formulas paper of Desrosiers–Lapointe–Mathieu and the Pieri-rules paper) and related Macdonald-superspace positivity conjectures, but no source confirming or refuting the integrality conjecture $v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)\in\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$ for the integral-form Jack superpolynomials was located. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Jack superpolynomials, superpartition ordering and determinantal formulas
status_evidence.snippet: Defines Jack polynomials in superspace as eigenfunctions of the supersymmetric Calogero–Moser–Sutherland model, triangular in the monomial basis.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background construction of Jack superpolynomials but does not establish the integrality of integral-form coefficients.

status_evidence.title: Pieri Rules for the Jack Polynomials in Superspace and the 6-Vertex Model
status_evidence.snippet: Pieri rules for Jack polynomials in superspace whose coefficients involve hook-length-type linear factors in alpha.
status_evidence.claim: Related structural results, but does not address the v_{ΛΩ}(α) ∈ Z[α] conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Macdonald Polynomials in Superspace: Conjectural Definition and Positivity Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectural Macdonald-in-superspace polynomials with positivity/integrality conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Macdonald-superspace analog of integrality conjectures remains conjectural; Jack-superspace integrality conjecture not confirmed proved here.
